SECURITY  BREACH
March 2020
Hackers has access to 95 million user profiles
Unresolved for 200 days
Negatively impacted Bumble’s public image and credibility

Brewster, Thomas. “Bumble Vulnerabilities Put Facebook Likes, Locations and Pictures of 95 Million Daters at Risk.” Forbes, 16 Nov. 2020, www.forbes.com/sites/thomasbrewster/2020/11/15/bumble-vulnerabilities-put-facebook-likes-locations-and-pictures-of-95-million-daters-at-risk/?sh=12103bcc3ddf.

Lack of accountability and transparency in periods of uncertainty  
Uncertainty Reduction Theory (Berger and Calabrese): 
High uncertainty → seek out information
Higher uncertainty = target less likeable 
Uncertainty Reduction Theory

BENEFITS &  DRAWBACKS
04

RECRUITING TALENTS
BENEFITS FOR USERS
FINDING MATCHES

MATCH
BUILDING CONNECTIONS
CONVERSATION
Bumble allows its users to read others’ profiles and choose whether to match with them
After a match is established, only female users can make the next step and decide whether they want to initiate the conversation
SUCCESS
Six months after the app had been founded, its female users have started more than one million conversations
Tepper, Fitz. “Bumble Dating App Tops 1 Million Unique Conversations.” TechCrunch, 11 June 2015, https://techcrunch.com/2015/06/11/bumble-dating-app-tops-1-million-unique-conversatio

FINDING MATCHES
Bumble allows users to add their basic information such as name, age, profession, height, star sign, education level, and up to six photos of their choice

Users with more extensive profiles better display their interests and personalities to other users, leading to more matches being made
“Bumble - Year in Review: What Worked Best on Bumble.” Bumble Buzz, https://bumble.com/the-buzz/year-in-review. Accessed 17 June 2023.

RECRUITING TALENT IN BUMBLE BIZZ
Bumble was not originally designed for recruiters to find candidates, but some entrepreneurs utilize it to reach out to as many people who might be interested as possible in a more casual way
Personalize business deals and make it a more creative and interesting process
Weiner, Zoë. “You Can Now Apply to Be Kris Jenner’s Personal Assistant.” Teen Vogue, 30 Apr. 2018, www.teenvogue.com/story/kris-jenner-bumble-bizz-assistant.

STEREOTYPES
Stereotype 
Truth
Casual sex rather than committed relationships

People use dating apps for a variety of reasons

Castro, Ángel, and Juan Ramón Barrada. “Dating Apps and Their Sociodemographic and Psychosocial Correlates: A Systematic Review.” International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health, U.S. National Library of Medicine, 7 Sept. 2020, www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC7557852/.

WHERE DO THESE STEREOTYPES STEM FROM?
CULTIVATION THEORY
Proposed by George Gerbner
Image of the world usually presented by the media — an “exaggeration or fantasy of what exists”
Many movies and TV shows portray dating apps as a way for people to find short-term relationships
Antidote: real-life experience 
Using dating apps
Cultural Communication. “Cultivation Theory.” Communication Theory, 27 Mar. 2015, www.communicationtheory.org/cultivation-theory/.

Bumble excels for its great functionalities, effectiveness in matching people for dates, and an emphasis on improving online dating experience for women
Bumble BFF and Bumble Bizz have great potential in expanding their influence
Despite the problems Bumble is facing, this revolutionary app still has a promising future
